paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: when you give something to the LORD, you MEAN it. A vow is not a loose thought you can swap out when a better deal walks by. The LORD says no trading good for bad or bad for good, and if you swap anyway, both animals become holy (Leviticus 27:10). Once I seal a cookie box, I don't sneak back in to swap the pretty cookies for the broken ones, and the LORD's people shouldn't either.

Some things were never ours to give in the first place. Firstborn livestock can't be consecrated, "because a firstborn belongs to the LORD" (Leviticus 27:26). The tithe is the same: "it is holy to the LORD" (Leviticus 27:30). I think that changes how a baker looks at giving, because the tithe isn't leftovers from our pile. It was the LORD's all along.

And the rules aren't cold. The one too poor to pay gets a price he can afford, because the priest sets the value by what he can manage (Leviticus 27:8). Then Leviticus closes with a reminder that these are the commandments the LORD gave to Moses for the Israelites on Mount Sinai (Leviticus 27:34). So keep your word, friend, give with a whole heart, and trust the LORD who made room for the poor.
